readme.html:
line-art-animation

An agent plugin and a small TypeScript library for animated line-art components: ink-on-paper figures that walk, ride and react, in scenes that run from day to night. Everything is drawn live in SVG, so it stays sharp at any size and responds to the pointer.

Day Night

What's in the repo
skills/line-art-animation/, references/ The skill: workflow, the rules that make the style work, and guides for style, motion, scenes, verification, matching a reference clip and rendering video.
lib/ Four dependency-free TypeScript modules: drawing primitives (ink.ts), a walk/run solver (gait.ts), springs, pendulums and wind (motion.ts), and a time-of-day palette (daynight.ts).
examples/walker/ One figure in about 150 lines: a man with a briefcase walks across the card; click him and he tips his hat.
examples/village/ A full scene: a street of machiya, a tea house and a bath house by a canal, villagers on schedules, a cat, birds, a boatman, lit windows and reflections, about a dozen interactions.
scripts/ Deterministic frame capture for video, and tools for measuring a reference clip.
mcp/server.mjs Local MCP server for browsing and reading the bundled kit.

Install the plugin

Clone this repository, or download it for clients other than Cursor. Run the commands below from the repository root, or replace "$PWD" with its absolute path. Node 22.18 or newer must be on the agent client's PATH. The skill and MCP server work without npm install.

Client Local installation
Codex Run codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD" and then codex plugin add line-art-animation@line-art-animation-kit. In the ChatGPT desktop app, install from Line-Art Animation Kit in the Plugins Directory.
Claude Code Run claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD" and then claude plugin install line-art-animation@line-art-animation-kit. For a one-session preview, use claude --plugin-dir "$PWD".
GitHub Copilot CLI Run copilot plugin marketplace add "$PWD" and then copilot plugin install line-art-animation@line-art-animation-kit.
VS Code Open Chat: Install Plugin from Source and select the checkout folder. For live development, add its absolute path with value true to chat.pluginLocations in Settings JSON.
Cursor Use the Cursor-native copy below, then reload Cursor and open Customize. Local plugin imports must be enabled.
Gemini CLI Run gemini extensions install "$PWD" and restart Gemini CLI.

Cursor uses its own MCP path variables. Run the following from a Git clone of this repository. The archive omits the portable manifests so Cursor loads its native configuration.

cursor_plugin="$HOME/.cursor/plugins/local/line-art-animation"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.cursor/plugins/local"
mkdir "$cursor_plugin" &&
  git archive HEAD -- . ':(exclude,top)plugin.json' ':(exclude,top)mcp.json' |
  tar -xf - -C "$cursor_plugin"

Start a new session and ask for an animation, for example:

  • “Make a line-art animation of a bakery at dawn with a baker carrying trays.”
  • “Turn this clip into a looping line-art component that matches its walk.”
  • “Add a day-night cycle and render a 30-second 1080p video.”

The plugin provides the line-art-animation skill. Its local MCP server exposes list_kit_files and read_kit_file for reading the guides, library, scripts, and examples. It uses stdio and does not require credentials or a network connection. Run builds, capture, and clip analysis in a writable project or checkout. The example preview needs npm dependencies, capture needs Chrome or Chromium, and video encoding and clip analysis need FFmpeg.

For a client without plugin support, install the full checkout under its skills directory, such as ~/.claude/skills/line-art-animation. The root SKILL.md loads the same workflow. For clients that register MCP servers separately, use command node with the absolute path to mcp/server.mjs as its only argument.

Check the server from a checkout with node --test mcp/server.test.mjs.

Run the examples

Requires Node 22.18 or newer.

npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173

In the village, drag the sun or moon across the sky to change the time, move the pointer to make wind, and click people, windows, lanterns, the wind chime, the cat, the birds or the water. URL flags: ?start=0.9 sets the starting time (0 is midnight, 0.5 noon), ?tau=0.5 pins it, ?day=30 makes a full day last 30 seconds, ?debug steps time by hand.

npm run typecheck  # strict for lib/ and the walker
npm run build

The library in brief

Figures are drawn in their own space, about 95 units tall with feet on y = 120, and placed into a scene with a transform. Limbs are two open pen strokes around a curve through the joints, which is most of what makes the drawing read as hand-inked.

A complete program that draws a pair of legs walking across the page (the walker example adds the body, arms, clothes and the click reaction):

import { el, limb, shoe, place, inkDefs, run } from './lib/ink.ts';
import { gait } from './lib/gait.ts';

const svg = el('svg', { viewBox: '0 0 480 240' });
document.body.append(svg);
const fig = el('g', { filter: inkDefs(svg).filter }, svg);
const legs = [limb(fig, 4.2), limb(fig, 4.2)];
const shoes = [el('path', {}, fig), el('path', {}, fig)];

const walk = gait({ kind: 'walk' });
let phase = 0, x = 60;
run((t, dt) => {
  phase += dt / walk.period;
  x += walk.speed * 1.25 * dt;           // move at the gait's speed and the feet stay planted
  place(fig, x % 520 - 20, 196, 1, 1.25);
  const p = walk.pose(phase);
  p.feet.forEach((foot, i) => {
    legs[i].draw([p.hip, foot.knee, foot.ankle]);
    shoe(shoes[i], foot.ankle, foot.pitch);
  });
});

gait() solves the legs rather than animating them: the planted foot slides back at exactly the travel speed, the swing follows a minimum-jerk path, the heel peels off the toe before each step, and hip height comes from what the planted legs can reach, so the body rises over each step and dips when both feet are down. Clothes are then drawn around the knees and ankles, so a coat or kimono opens and closes with the stride.

palette(τ) gives sky, paper and ink colours for any time of day. Ink is currentColor and paper fills carry a pp class, so applyPalette() can turn the whole drawing into pale ink on indigo at night while windows and lanterns glow.

Render a video

npm run dev
node scripts/capture.ts "http://localhost:5173/examples/village/?debug&capture&day=30&start=0.3" \
  captures/village 900 30 1920 1080
ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i captures/village/f%04d.png -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 15 \
  -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -tune animation village.mp4

The capture script drives headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, with no npm dependencies, and advances the scene by exactly one frame between screenshots, so the result doesn't depend on machine speed. It finds a local Chrome or Chromium, or uses $CHROME. The video encoding step uses FFmpeg.

Match a reference clip

node scripts/clip.ts period clip.mp4 X Y W H          # loop length of a region
node scripts/clip.ts blobs clip.mp4 X Y W H Y0 Y1     # dark blobs per frame, e.g. feet
scripts/frames.sh clip.mp4 X Y W H out/               # frames with a measuring grid

references/matching.md covers the rest: why to resample by time (most social clips are variable-frame-rate), reading poses off the grid, and an overlay mode for checking your drawing against the clip.
